1. Overview 
The Grievance Window is a dedicated module within Vedika Health that provides a structured, 
trackable channel for users to raise complaints, share feedback, and report issues. It replaces 
ad-hoc communication (phone, email) with a formal system that ensures accountability, 
transparency, and measurable resolution timelines. Module Goals 
Enable patients, doctors, and vendors to submit structured grievances with supporting evidence.

Module Goals 
Enable patients, doctors, and vendors to submit structured grievances with supporting evidence. Give the Master Admin full visibility, triage capability, and a response workflow. Generate metrics (volume, resolution time, category breakdown) to drive quality improvements. Trigger real-time notifications to both parties on every status change.

Trigger real-time notifications to both parties on every status change. Scope 
This document covers the end-to-end implementation of the Grievance Window across all three 
platforms: 
• vedika-health-app — Flutter mobile application (patient-facing) 
• vedika-health-web — React / TypeScript web application (patient + admin) 
• Backend REST API — to be implemented alongside the frontend modules 
 
Out of Scope (v1.0) 
• Third-party ombudsman integration 
• Automated resolution via AI triage (planned v2.0) 
• Grievance analytics dashboard with charts (planned v2.0)

2. User Flows 
2.1 Patient / User Flow 
The following steps describe the complete journey a patient takes from discovering the 
grievance feature to tracking its resolution. # Step Detail 
1 Navigate to Grievances Accessible via bottom navigation bar (mobile) or left sidebar 
(web). Visible to all verified users. 2 Grievance list screen Displays all previous grievances as cards with GRV-ID, title, 
category, date, and colour-coded status badge.

3 Tap 'Raise New 
Grievance' 
Opens the new grievance form. Button is prominent and 
always visible. 4 Complete the form 
User selects category, enters title and description (minimum 
50 characters), optionally links an appointment/clinic, sets 
priority, and attaches up to 5 files. 5 Submit System creates the grievance with status PENDING. A push 
notification and in-app alert confirm submission. 6 Track progress 
User views the detail screen to see the full conversation 
thread, status history, and admin replies. Reply box is disabled 
once status is CLOSED.

Key Screens (User) • Grievance List Screen — card layout, status badges (red = pending, orange = under review, green = resolved), pull-to-refresh, pagination • New Grievance Form — category dropdown, title field, description textarea, related-to auto-suggest, file picker (max 5 files, image/PDF only), priority chip selector • Grievance Detail Screen — chronological message thread (user messages left, admin replies right), status history timeline, add-reply box 2.2 Master Admin Flow The Master Admin accesses the grievance module from the admin dashboard and manages the complete lifecycle of
every grievance raised across the platform.

3. Status Lifecycle & Priority 
3.1 Status Values 
Each grievance progresses through a defined sequence of statuses. Transitions are one-
directional with the exception that UNDER_REVIEW can be reopened to PENDING if additional 
information is needed. PENDING Newly submitted. No admin action taken yet. UNDER_REVIEW Admin has acknowledged and is investigating. RESOLVED Issue addressed. Resolution date logged. CLOSED Finalised. No further replies accepted.

RESOLVED Issue addressed. Resolution date logged. CLOSED Finalised. No further replies accepted. 3.2 Priority Levels 
Priority is set by the user at submission time and can be overridden by the admin. It determines 
sort order in the admin table and drives SLA targets. HIGH Doctor behaviour, billing disputes, safety complaints. Target SLA: < 4 hours. MEDIUM General appointment issues, consultation quality. Target SLA: < 24 hours. LOW Technical glitches, suggestions, minor inconveniences. Target SLA: < 72 hours.

4.2 Category Enum Values 
The following categories are available for selection at submission time. This list is returned by 
the GET /api/grievances/categories endpoint and should be populated dynamically in all 
dropdowns.

• Appointment Related 
• Billing / Payment Issue 
• Doctor Behaviour 
• Clinic Facility / Hygiene 
• Consultation Quality 
• Technical / App Issue 
• Refund Request 
• Others 
 
4.3 Response Thread Schema 
Each entry in the responses array follows this structure: 
 
Field Type Description 
timestamp Timestamp UTC timestamp of when the reply was submitted 
message Text The reply content 
byAdmin Boolean true if authored by an admin user, false if by the patient 
authorId String User ID or Admin ID of the author

5. API Specification 
All endpoints use JSON (application/json) unless noted as multipart. All user endpoints require a 
valid Bearer token. Admin endpoints additionally require the MASTER_ADMIN role checked 
server-side. 5.1 User APIs 
Available to authenticated patients, doctors, and vendors. Each user sees only their own 
grievances.

6.

Frontend Design Specifications 6.1 User Side (App + Web) Grievance List Screen • Card layout — one card per grievance • Each card shows: GRV-ID, title (truncated at 60 chars), category tag, submission date, and status badge • Status badge colours: red (#E24B4A) = PENDING, orange (#EF9F27) = UNDER_REVIEW, green (#3B6D11) = RESOLVED, grey = CLOSED • Pull-to-refresh on mobile; infinite scroll or pagination (10 per page) on web • 'Raise New Grievance' floating action button (mobile) or header button (web) — always visible New Grievance Form • Category — required dropdown, values from GET

/api/grievances/categories • Title — text field, max 120 characters, character counter visible • Description — textarea, minimum 50 characters enforced on submit with inline error • Related to — optional auto-suggest field pre-populated with the user's recent appointments • File upload — native file picker, image/PNG, image/JPEG, PDF only, max 5 MB per file, max 5 files • Priority — chip selector (Low / Medium / High), default Medium • Submit button — large, full-width on mobile, disabled until required fields are valid Grievance Detail Screen • Chronological message thread: user messages

aligned left, admin replies aligned right with a blue left border accent • Each message shows: author label, timestamp, message text • Status change events appear as system messages in the thread (e.g.

'Status changed to 
UNDER_REVIEW — 21 Apr 2026') 
• Reply text input + Send button visible at the bottom; hidden (not just disabled) when 
status = CLOSED

Grievance Dashboard

Time (hrs)

7. Implementation Plan 
Implementation follows a backend-first approach to unblock both frontend teams in parallel. Each phase has a defined checklist and acceptance criteria.

Phase 1 — Backend (Week 1–2) ☐ Create Grievance model and run database migration ☐ Implement auto-generation of human-readable GRV-ID on INSERT ☐ Implement all 4 user-facing REST endpoints with proper auth middleware ☐ Implement all 5 admin REST endpoints with MASTER_ADMIN role guard ☐ Multipart file upload support (reuse clinic registration pattern); store to cloud storage ☐ Implement notification service triggers for all 6 events (Section 5.3) ☐ Write unit tests for status transition validation (reject invalid transitions server -side) ☐ API documentation (Swagger / Postman collection)

shared with frontend teams Phase 2 — User Frontend: Flutter App (Week 2–3) ☐ Add 'Grievances' tab to bottom navigation bar ☐ Implement Grievance List screen with card layout and status badges ☐ Implement pull-to-refresh and infinite scroll/pagination ☐ Implement New Grievance Form with all fields and client-side validation ☐ Implement file picker with type/size restrictions and preview ☐ Implement Grievance Detail screen with conversation thread ☐ Integrate all 4 user APIs ☐ Handle push notification deep links to the correct grievance detail screen Phase 3 — User Frontend: React Web (Week
2–3, parallel) ☐ Add 'Grievances' entry to the left sidebar with unread badge count ☐ Implement Grievance List page (mirrors Flutter screen, adapted for web layout)

9. Next Steps & Prompts 
The following ready-to-use prompts can be passed directly to Cursor, Antigravity, or any AI 
coding assistant to generate implementation artefacts. Generate: Backend Model + Migration 
Create the Grievances database model and migration based on the schema in Section 4, 
including indexes on userId, status, priority, and createdAt. Generate: All REST API Controllers 
Implement all 9 endpoints from Section 5 using the existing Vedika Health API patterns.

Include 
role-based middleware, multipart file handling, and notification triggers. Generate: Flutter Screens 
Build the three Flutter screens (Grievance List, New Grievance Form, Grievance Detail) following 
the design specs in Section 6.1. Use the existing design system and integrate the 4 user APIs. Generate: Admin React Components 
Build the Grievance Dashboard, All Grievances Table, and Grievance Detail Modal in 
React/TypeScript following Section 6.2. Integrate all 5 admin APIs.
